scenes.tts: Two neighbouring cells in a chick spinal cord make the same protein. One becomes a motor neuron, the other an interneuron. How?
scenes.visual: Title card: One Protein, Two Cell Types. A transverse section of the spinal cord with two neighbouring cells lit in the same colour, each labelled with a question mark.
scenes.narration: Two neighbouring cells in a chick spinal cord make the same protein. One becomes a motor neuron, the other an interneuron. How?

scenes.tts: The protein is L H X three. Both newly born motor neurons and V two interneurons make it.
scenes.caption: The protein is Lhx3. Both newly born motor neurons and V2 interneurons make it.
scenes.visual: The two cells labelled: lower cell 'newly born motor neuron', upper cell 'V2 interneuron'. Both carry the same orange protein, labelled Lhx3.
scenes.narration: The protein is Lhx3. Both newly born motor neurons and V2 interneurons make it.

scenes.tts: A second protein, Islet one, is made in the motor neurons, not the V two interneurons.
scenes.caption: A second protein, Isl1, is made in the motor neurons, not the V2 interneurons.
scenes.visual: A blue protein, labelled Isl1, appears only in the lower cell.
scenes.narration: A second protein, Isl1, is made in the motor neurons, not the V2 interneurons.

scenes.tts: Both are Lim homeodomain proteins. The homeodomain binds DNA. Two Lim domains are handles that other proteins grip.
scenes.caption: Both are LIM homeodomain proteins. The homeodomain binds DNA. Two LIM domains are handles that other proteins grip.
scenes.visual: Close-up of Lhx3 drawn as a block: a homeodomain resting on a DNA strand, and two LIM domains drawn as handles sticking up. Labels: homeodomain binds DNA; LIM domains bind proteins (handles).
scenes.narration: Both are LIM homeodomain proteins. The homeodomain binds DNA. Two LIM domains are handles that other proteins grip.

scenes.tts: A third player, the cofactor N L I, binds no DNA. It pairs with itself and grips Lim domains.
scenes.caption: A third player, the cofactor NLI, binds no DNA. It pairs with itself and grips LIM domains.
scenes.visual: A grey clip labelled NLI (also called Ldb1). Two clips snap together into a pair. Label: no DNA-binding domain.
scenes.narration: A third player, the cofactor NLI, binds no DNA. It pairs with itself and grips LIM domains.

scenes.tts: Predict. Put L H X three alone into chick cells without Islet one. Then put in both. Which genes come up?
scenes.caption: Predict. Put Lhx3 alone into chick cells without Isl1. Then put in both. Which genes come up?
scenes.visual: A chick embryo with one side of the neural tube electroporated (green). Two panels: A, Lhx3 alone; B, Lhx3 plus Isl1. Three answer chips: motor-neuron genes (Mnx1), V2 genes (Chx10), neither.
scenes.narration: Predict. Put Lhx3 alone into chick cells without Isl1. Then put in both. Which genes come up?

scenes.tts: Alone, it turns on V two interneuron genes, such as C H X ten.
scenes.caption: Alone, it turns on V2 interneuron genes, such as Chx10.
scenes.visual: Panel A lights: the V2 gene Chx10 glows. No motor-neuron gene.
scenes.narration: Alone, it turns on V2 interneuron genes, such as Chx10.

scenes.tts: With Islet one, it turns on motor neuron genes, such as M N X one. V two genes are largely held down.
scenes.caption: With Isl1, it turns on motor-neuron genes, such as Mnx1. V2 genes are largely held down.
scenes.visual: Panel B lights: Mnx1 glows; Chx10 is dimmed, not off, with a down arrow.
scenes.narration: With Isl1, it turns on motor-neuron genes, such as Mnx1. V2 genes are largely held down.

scenes.tts: Why? Without Islet one, N L I grips L H X three directly. Pairs of these units bind V two genes.
scenes.caption: Why? Without Isl1, NLI grips Lhx3 directly. Pairs of these units bind V2 genes.
scenes.visual: Upper cell: the NLI clip grips both Lhx3 handles. Two NLI and Lhx3 units pair through the clips and sit on a gene labelled V2 genes. Credit: Thaler et al., 2002.
scenes.narration: Why? Without Isl1, NLI grips Lhx3 directly. Pairs of these units bind V2 genes.

scenes.tts: With Islet one present, Islet one grips N L I itself. Then it holds L H X three on a short segment.
scenes.caption: With Isl1 present, Isl1 grips NLI itself. Then it holds Lhx3 on a short segment.
scenes.visual: Lower cell: Isl1 takes the NLI clip with its own handles. A short tail on Isl1 wraps around the Lhx3 handles.
scenes.narration: With Isl1 present, Isl1 grips NLI itself. Then it holds Lhx3 on a short segment.

scenes.tts: Pairs of this three part complex promote motor neuron genes.
scenes.visual: Two three-part units, NLI, Isl1 and Lhx3, pair through the clips and sit on a gene labelled motor-neuron genes. The cell is labelled motor neuron.
scenes.narration: Pairs of this three part complex promote motor neuron genes.

scenes.tts: N L I is in both. What differs is the bridge, Islet one.
scenes.caption: NLI is in both. What differs is the bridge, Isl1.
scenes.visual: Side by side: the two complexes. NLI highlighted in both. The Isl1 bridge highlighted in the motor-neuron complex only.
scenes.narration: NLI is in both. What differs is the bridge, Isl1.

scenes.tts: Does any Islet one at all give a clean switch? Try a simple binding model.
scenes.caption: Does any Isl1 at all give a clean switch? Try a simple binding model.
scenes.visual: A slider labelled Isl1 relative to Lhx3. Banner: ideal binding model, not a measurement.
scenes.narration: Does any Isl1 at all give a clean switch? Try a simple binding model.

scenes.tts: With equal amounts, about a quarter of the L H X three still sits in the interneuron complex.
scenes.caption: With equal amounts, about a quarter of the Lhx3 still sits in the interneuron complex.
scenes.visual: Slider at 'equal'. A bar for Lhx3: 24% in V2 units, 37% in motor-neuron units, the rest free or held by Isl1 alone. Legible model caption: equal binding strengths; Lhx3 and NLI at ten times the dissociation constant; single units, no DNA. Label: model.
scenes.narration: With equal amounts, about a quarter of the Lhx3 still sits in the interneuron complex.

scenes.tts: Less Islet one leaves more. In this model, binding alone gives a mixture, not a switch.
scenes.caption: Less Isl1 leaves more. In this model, binding alone gives a mixture, not a switch.
scenes.visual: Slider slides to 'half as much': V2 45%, motor-neuron 23%. Then to 'none': V2 73%, motor-neuron 0%. Label: model.
scenes.narration: Less Isl1 leaves more. In this model, binding alone gives a mixture, not a switch.

scenes.tts: The model does not decide a cell's fate. In real cells, a downstream regulator helps lock the choice in.
scenes.visual: A padlock icon appears beside the motor-neuron cell, with a question mark. Label: shown by separate experiments (chapter 2).
scenes.narration: The model does not decide a cell's fate. In real cells, a downstream regulator helps lock the choice in.

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea to carry. No single factor says motor neuron.
scenes.visual: Callout card: The one idea. No single factor says motor neuron.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea to carry. No single factor says motor neuron.

scenes.tts: Here, identity depends on which complexes form. That depends on which partners are present, and in what ratio.
scenes.visual: The callout card completes: identity depends on which complexes form; those depend on which partners, and in what ratio.
scenes.narration: Here, identity depends on which complexes form. That depends on which partners are present, and in what ratio.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: one protein, held by different partners, builds two different cells.
scenes.visual: Closing card: one protein, two partners, two cells.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: one protein, held by different partners, builds two different cells.
